content.value_statement: Consent evidence and withdrawal events can become inconsistent across email systems. This skill records pseudonymous consent facts and prioritizes live suppression checks before downstream use.
actual_capabilities: Records opt-in facts with source, timestamp, lawful-basis, and proof references.
Checks whether a pseudonymous subject is currently suppressed.
Prioritizes unsubscribe, complaint, and hard-bounce suppression events.
Defines authorization requirements for opt-in, restore, and erasure actions.
Prepares a structured handoff when the trusted registry runtime is unavailable.
limitations: It does not send email or edit email service provider state.
It requires a trusted host capability for opt-in, restore, and erasure mutations.
It stores pseudonymous IDs and proof pointers, not raw contact details.
It cannot claim canonical registry state without the verified runtime and schema.

use_cases.title: Record verified opt-in evidence
use_cases.description: Capture a pseudonymous subject, source, timestamp, lawful basis, and proof reference for an authorized subscription.

use_cases.title: Process immediate withdrawal
use_cases.description: Record an unsubscribe, complaint, or hard bounce and verify that the live suppression result is active.

use_cases.title: Review consent status before a campaign
use_cases.description: Query current suppression status for a pseudonymous subject instead of relying on cached segment data.

prompt_templates.title: Check suppression status
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether pseudonymous subject <subject-id> is currently suppressed. Report the result and any missing evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Record an opt-in
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare an authorized opt-in record for <subject-id> using source <source>, timestamp <timestamp>, lawful basis <basis>, and proof reference <proof-ref>. Do not include raw contact data.

prompt_templates.title: Handle an unsubscribe
prompt_templates.prompt: Process this unsubscribe for <subject-id> from event <event-id> at <timestamp>. Apply immediate suppression, then state how to verify the live result.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare an erasure handoff
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare the required authorized erasure handoff for <subject-id>. Identify only the fields that are missing and do not claim that a mutation occurred.

output_examples.input: Is subject sha256-7d9f suppressed right now?
output: Use the live registry replay result before any downstream email action.

output_examples.input: Record an unsubscribe for subject sha256-7d9f from webhook evt-882.
output: Immediate suppression handoff prepared for sha256-7d9f.
Confirm the live suppression projection after the authorized append completes.

best_practices: Use pseudonymous subject IDs and minimum proof references only.
Check the live suppression result before email eligibility or delivery work.
Require fresh, authorized evidence before restoring a withdrawn subscription.
anti_patterns: Do not store raw email addresses, names, or phone numbers in registry events.
Do not infer consent when lawful-basis evidence is missing.
Do not manually edit projections or clear suppression state.

faq.question: Does this skill send email?
faq.answer: No. It records consent evidence and suppression state only.

faq.question: Can it store email addresses?
faq.answer: No. It is designed for pseudonymous IDs and minimum proof pointers.

faq.question: What happens after an unsubscribe?
faq.answer: The workflow prioritizes immediate suppression and requires verification of the live result.

faq.question: Can a user restore a subscription?
faq.answer: Only with a trusted host capability and fresh opt-in evidence after the withdrawal.

faq.question: Can this skill erase records?
faq.answer: It can prepare or execute an authorized erasure workflow through the trusted host runtime.

faq.question: Does it determine campaign eligibility?
faq.answer: No. It provides live suppression status for downstream systems to use.
